key_insight: A weak, low-frequency forcing barely changes the jet’s mean development but strongly alters turbulence scales and boosts inertial-particle clustering in a phase-dependent way.
engineering_relevance: This suggests periodic modulation can be used as a control knob to tune mixing and particle organization in jets without major changes to the mean flow.
method: Hot-wire anemometry measured carrier-flow turbulence in a periodically forced planar jet.
High-speed particle imaging tracked dilute inertial droplets.
Voronoi tessellations quantified preferential concentration and its variation over the forcing cycle.
evidence_signal: Across two Reynolds numbers (~4950 and ~9900), forcing reduced the integral scale by up to 40% and changed clustering by 21–49% of its cycle mean, while the mean-flow evolution stayed nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The control effect is strongly phase dependent, so conclusions based on cycle-averaged quantities can miss large instantaneous changes in clustering and dissipation.
paper_title: Preferential concentration in a periodically forced particle-laden turbulent planar jet
